Phase states and phase transitions (10.0 points) At a given pressure, the transition from one phase state of matter to another always occurs at a strictly defined temperature, and the transition itself is called a phase transition. For example, ice at atmospheric pressure melts at 0 ℃, so that when the heat is supplied, the temperature of the mixture of ice and water remains unchanged until all the ice turns into water.

entries.source: Tetrachloromethane or hydrogen tetrachloride is a heavy (density [[0]] ) transparent liquid with a molar mass [[1]] . A vessel with a volume of [[3]] is half-filled with the carbon tetrachloride, and the same (by volume) amount of water is poured over it.
